Done. The GOLD tier rule is implemented with minimal structural impact — three files touched, no method grown, no change to any large class:

1. **`OwnerHouseholdPolicy.java`** — one line: every created owner now gets its deterministic `householdId` (previously only the second-and-later member of a shared household did), so all members of a household share the same id. Duplicate-rejection behavior is unchanged.

2. **`OwnerHouseholdTierPostProcessor.java`** (new, tiny cohesive unit) — a MapStruct `@AfterMapping` component that counts owners sharing the owner's `householdId` and upgrades `membershipTier` to `GOLD` when there are 3 or more.

3. **`OwnerMapper.java`** — one annotation edit adding the post-processor to `uses`, so MapStruct invokes it after the existing BRONZE/SILVER expression.

The GOLD check overrides the BRONZE/SILVER result (GOLD takes precedence); when the household has fewer than 3 members the existing rules stand. Because the tier is derived at read time from the persisted `householdId`, it works across separate transactions and on every configured database with no schema or seed-data changes.
